title: Astrid y Gastón Opened French and Became Peruvian One Dish at a Time
thinker: Zhuangzi (words given to Prince Mou of Wei)
conflicts: Acurio's own accounts of when the menu turned Peruvian differ: 'almost from the first day', little by little (2014 letter); 'one day it all changed' with a strategy 'after a couple of years' (2016 interview); defined as Peruvian haute cuisine after five years (2006 speech). The story presents a gradual change and uses the five-year figure for the redefinition, attributed to the 2006 speech.
notes: Key founder sources are in Spanish (2014 farewell letter on RPP, 2006 Universidad del Pacífico speech, 2005 Andina profile) and are paraphrased, not quoted; the only quoted founder words are from the English Daily Meal interview. Three sources are Internet Archive copies; web.archive.org was intermittently unreachable during research, but all loaded on the final check. Funding was US$45,000 lent by relatives and friends.
